# Third party licenses and notices

Aurora Lights original code remains MIT licensed. Dependencies, runtimes, fonts and game content retain their own licenses. This inventory currently covers the Windows x64 and Android ARM64 release dependency set; Windows ARM64 and macOS remain experimental, and Web remains deferred.

`components.json` records exact versions, applicable platforms, source references, copyright metadata, legal-text hashes and unresolved release issues. `texts/` preserves the legal texts, including upstream third-party notices. The inventory conservatively includes build dependencies as well as runtime dependencies. A license expression alone does not establish that all distribution obligations have been met.

`assets.json` separately records the bundled content/artwork/fonts and additional legacy/branding assets included with corresponding source. Each file has a SHA-256, review group and actual distribution scopes. Recorded font groups are tied to the matching component license and binary hash. Pending groups record missing evidence, not a grant to redistribute. See [the content and asset review](../docs/bundled-content-and-assets-2026-10-23.md) for the completed migration, permission basis and validation results.

Run `python tools/licensing/build_notices.py` after reviewing changes to the inventory. This regenerates the offline pages and complete text bundle under `Aurora.App/wwwroot/legal/`. The application serves these packaged files from About, without a network request. Ordinary local builds do not clear licensing for distribution.

Run `python tools/licensing/build_notices.py --check` to verify the text hashes and generated files. For dependency coverage, add `--platform windows --dependencies <published Aurora.Reflections.deps.json>` or `--platform android --dependencies <Aurora.App/obj/project.assets.json>`. Both formats are supported. The release workflow also uses `--require-resolved`; it rejects pending records/issues and previously unrecorded dependency versions before packaging/upload.

The same command verifies asset inventory coverage and hashes. Review new/changed files before updating those records; do not bulk refresh hashes to bypass a provenance change. `python -m unittest discover -s tools/licensing -p "test_*.py"` runs the focused gate regressions. Release source bundles additionally use `build_source_bundle.py --require-resolved` so permissions for source-only assets cannot be bypassed by passing native-package checks. Non-strict local source bundles remain review artifacts and do not establish distribution clearance.

When a dependency changes, obtain its exact package metadata and complete license/NOTICE files, review bundled native or Java components, preserve copyright notices, and update the record and text hashes. Retain a source/version reference. Do not replace vendor license terms with a guessed SPDX identifier or treat an HTTP success page as a license. Review runtime-pack notices and embedded assets separately from the managed-package list. The collection evidence and isolated PDF replacement experiments are under `artifacts/licensing-2026-10-23/`.

## Current release status

The shipping projects now use iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core 3.8.6 (LGPL-2.0-only). Original Aurora code remains MIT. See [LGPL-RELINKING.md](LGPL-RELINKING.md) for the prominent library notice, modification rights, exact corresponding source and rebuild/relink instructions. The full upstream source archive is pinned and hashed in `sources/manifest.json`. The release workflow creates `aurora-corresponding-source.zip` and attaches it alongside the native downloads. Redistributors must preserve equivalent access to matching source materials.

The old AGPL iTextSharp 5.5.13 DLL remains under `lib/` solely for immutable historical oracle tests. No shipping project references it. Its attribution is retained in `legacy-test-only.json` and legal texts; it is omitted from the shipping inventory/source bundle. Do not use it to build/distribute the migrated application. The comparison harness compiles the same document assertions separately against each engine.

Aurora.Content and Aurora.Content.Contracts are explicitly MIT licensed by the owner in `vendor/nuget/LICENSE-Aurora.Content.txt`; their original nupkg bytes remain unchanged. The remaining asset/content inventory is now resolved for the reviewed resource versions: legacy redistribution permissions and original branding are recorded, standalone fonts have independent grants, and non-SRD game definitions/prose have been removed or replaced. The new baseline and import boundary are documented in `CONTENT-SCOPE.md`, `srd-baseline.json` and `srd-spells.json`. The PDF migration's acceptance evidence is recorded in the PDF migration review; do not infer overall v1.0 distribution approval from a passing compile.

The Win2D package's published license URL redirects to an unrelated Microsoft documentation page. The official Win2D README identifies the NuGet project as MIT; the reviewed upstream MIT license is included at a fixed source commit. Xamarin.Build.Download's retired file link is replaced by the project's main MIT license, alongside its package third-party notices. The existing OGL 1.0a text and Section 15 SRD copyright notice are preserved without asserting a grant for unrelated gallery art, branding or templates.

The public 1.0 preparation baseline contains 319 SRD spells, with canonical SRD names and preserved compatibility identifiers. Existing characters or imports are not rewritten. Characters that need excluded definitions must have their corresponding content loaded; partial-load diagnostics remain active. Both strict native checks and the source-bundle check must pass for each new release build. This inventory does not validate previously built RC1 packages against the new baseline.
